- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.3) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model often overcorrects downward; cap downward correction at 10% of spike magnitude.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.7) and price is trending up, model frequently overestimates; apply downward bias of 1–3% to forecast.
- Model underestimates mean-reverting periods (e.g., after 75+ peak) — if 3 consecutive days show price < 70, adjust forecast downward by 1–4%.
- Forecast horizon 30d often exhibits lag: if true outcome shows strong downward trend after 10–15 days, model still holds upward bias — reduce forecast by 2–5% from day 10 onward.
- When sentiment history shows alternating high/low (e.g., 0.8, 0.2, 0.8), model overfits to recent sentiment — dampen forecast by 1–3% if sentiment swings sharply.
